first_falsifiers.statement: Zed-style mutable state, PR numbers, or current frontier fields appear inside the stable graph; static validation must fail.
A controller, proof, fan-in, or governance node is made buildable and enters a builder frontier; validation must fail.
Issue numbers are used as semantic node identity, so decomposing or superseding an issue silently moves graph identity; stable IDs plus explicit references must be used instead.
Domain policy owned by a canonical issue is copied into programme-local prose or payloads instead of being referenced; validation must fail.
A required accepted-store consumer row is removed while the consumer cutover proposition remains; fan-in validation must fail.
A controller is marked satisfied from child count alone without its own integration row; fan-in validation must fail.
The optional live observer becomes a hard dependency of offline frontier, packet, or closeout work; validation must fail.
Two unordered nodes declare parallel work over the same exclusive conflict key such as config.authority_catalog or close.evaluator; validation must fail.
Serialization is inferred from file overlap alone, or same-authority work in disjoint files is declared parallel; semantic conflict keys must govern instead.
Retirement is represented without predecessor identity, current consumers, and exit condition; validation must fail.
A leaf is permitted to terminate its controller without an explicit contract; relation validation must fail.
A required artifact has no canonical owner node; validation must fail.
Current proof verdicts or tree movement change stable graph bytes; the graph must remain byte-identical while projections move instead.
The parser defaults or ignores an unknown edge, profile, or node field instead of failing closed.
Input or map ordering changes normalized output; repeated normalization must be byte-identical.
Malformed, truncated, or otherwise unavailable graph input resolves to an empty valid graph instead of an instrument failure.
